newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Oct trade deficit seen near Sept's-report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Oct trade deficit seen near Sept's-report.

text.p: Brazilian Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said Monday the trade deficit in October is expected to be no higher than September's $655 million gap, the local Invest News agency reported.
Invest News reported the minister said while on a visit to Sao Paulo that the government was studying about 10 measures that could be implemented to boost exports.
"Operational issues are impeding growth in exports," it quoted him as saying at a seminar, adding he could guarantee October's gap would not be larger than September's.

Kandir, calling concern about Brazil's trade performance "excessive," said Brasilia was studying changes to export credit lines issued by the National Development Bank (BNDES) and an alternative to surcharges levied by banks on export finance.
Invest News did not report on the other measures the government was studying to boost overseas sales.
"We are studying ways of spreading the risk," Kandir said.
October exports were due to be announced on Tuesday while the trade balance will be revealed around mid-month.
